articles.title: Mudryk regresa tras dos años de sanción y se va cedido al Tottenham de su 'padre' Roberto de Zerbi
articles.standfirst: El ucraniano regresa a la competición tras cumplir la sanción impuesta por el TAS y se reencuentra con Roberto de Zerbi, con quien coincidió en el Shakhtar Donest
articles.summary: El ucraniano regresa a la competición tras cumplir la sanción impuesta por el TAS y se reencuentra con Roberto de Zerbi, con quien coincidió en el Shakhtar Donest
articles.body: El Tottenham ha cerrado en las horas finales del mercado la cesión de Mykhailo Mudryk procedente del Chelsea, en una operación sin opción de compra que se prolongará hasta el final de la temporada 2026/27. El extremo ucraniano se convierte en otra de las grandes incorporaciones que ha cosechado el club spur de cara a este curso, uno de los que más ha renovado su plantilla sin lugar a dudas en la Premier. El movimiento pone fin a un culebrón que se había alargado buena parte del verano, con varias ofertas, no ya del Tottenham, sino del Leeds United, todas rechazadas por el Chelsea. Al final ha sido el equipo de Roberto de Zerbi, con quien, además, coincidió el extremo ucraniano en su etapa del Shakhtar Donest. Para Mudryk, de 25 años, esta cesión supone sobre todo una oportunidad de recuperar continuidad. El futbolista no disputaba un partido oficial desde el 28 de noviembre de 2024, cuando participó en la victoria del Chelsea por 2-0 ante el Heidenheim en la Conference League. Un mes después, en diciembre, dio positivo por meldonium en un control antidopaje, lo que derivó en una suspensión provisional y, finalmente, en una sanción de cuatro años impuesta por el TAS. El pasado julio, sin embargo, la Football Association inglesa llegó a un acuerdo con la Agencia Mundial Antidopaje: la normativa había sido actualizada y, con la concentración de meldonium detectada en su día, hoy esa muestra no habría derivado en sanción. La FA confirmó entonces que Mudryk quedaba habilitado para volver a competir con efecto inmediato. El ucraniano reapareció en un amistoso de pretemporada ante la Juventus el pasado 5 de agosto, aunque sin haber vuelto a jugar un partido de competición oficial desde hace prácticamente dos años. "Es con otro hijo. Estoy muy feliz. Se merece jugar. Esperemos que esta temporada pueda demostrar lo que ha pasado en los últimos años. Quizás no contra el Tottenham, en un jugador top", dijo recientemente Roberto de Zerbi sobre Misha Mudryk, que quien llegó a decir hace unos años que el ucraniano podría ser perfectamente Balón de Oro. El Chelsea pagó en enero de 2023 alrededor de 70 millones de euros al Shakhtar Donetsk por hacerse con sus servicios, una cifra que en su momento lo convirtió en uno de los fichajes más caros de la historia del club. En sus tres años en Stamford Bridge, Mudryk disputó 73 partidos y anotó 10 goles, lejos de las expectativas generadas por su traspaso. Ahora, con contrato en Londres hasta 2031, el objetivo del club blue es que recupere ritmo competitivo antes de decidir su futuro a largo plazo.

articles.title: El Leganés cierra la puerta a la llegada de Carvajal
articles.standfirst: Andrés Pardo, director de fútbol del club pepinero, da la plantilla por cerrada
articles.summary: Andrés Pardo, director de fútbol del club pepinero, da la plantilla por cerrada
articles.body: El Leganés no dará otro bombazo con Dani Carvajal. Al menos es lo que se desprende de las palabras de Andrés Pardo el último día del mercado. El director deportivo del cuadro pepinero habló ante los medios presentes en la sede de LaLiga por medio de videollamada y explicó, además del posible fichaje de Carvajal, la llegada de Álvaro Morata. Aunque Carvajal podría llegar después del cierre del mercado, al estar sin equipo, Andrés Pardo habló de plantilla cerada. Fichaje Morata: "E n la secretaría técnica y dirección deportiva, estábamos buscando un perfil de delantero muy top y queríamos optar a lo máximo Fue una situación en la que como os podéis imaginar, cuando se plantea inicialmente en nuestro interior, cuando nosotros mismos nos dijimos el nombre de Álvaro, dijimos esto es una pedrada imposible. Parecía muy muy imposible pero después se fue avanzando, tuvimos un primer contacto muy positivo, a él se le veía muy ilusionado desde el principio. Han sido semanas de muchos contactos, llamadas a diversas horas, por la mañana y por la noche y hemos conseguido que uno de los delanteros muy importantes a nivel europeo de los últimos tiempos pueda jugar en el Leganés. Muy orgulloso en el club y muy orgullosos de Álvaro". Fair Play: "Es cierto que nosotros, tanto el club como la propiedad, veníamos de una temporada que hemos acumulado mucho daño. No competimos bien. Y esta temporada hemos sido muy ambiciosos, muy exigentes, hemos ido todos a una. Queríamos una revolución y hemos firmado dos jugadores que venían de jugar el mundial. Hemos hecho hasta 12-13 fichajes y a nivel de Fair Play hemos ido equilibrando las cuentas. En eso el club hace un trabajo increíble y todo lo que hemos podido proponer se ha podido llevar a cabo". ¿Carvajal es posible? "Me habéis puesto el listón muy alto, demasiado alto. Parece que firmamos a Álvaro hace semanas y lo presentamos el viernes. Desde el sábado y el domingo todo el mundo me dice lo mismo, que es lo que comentabas. A este nivel doy la plantilla por cerrada a estas horas, tenemos a dos jugadores por puesto y estamos contentos con la confección de plantilla y no nos vamos a mover nada".

articles.title: El Elche incorpora a Lemar para reforzar su centro del campo
articles.standfirst: El francés llega cedido por el Atlético y se convierte en la octava cara nueva y el tercer fichaje franjiverde del último día del mercado
articles.summary: El francés llega cedido por el Atlético y se convierte en la octava cara nueva y el tercer fichaje franjiverde del último día del mercado
articles.body: El Elche ha hecho oficial la incorporación de Thomas Lemar, que llega cedido por el Atlético de Madrid. El centrocampista francés se convierte en la octava cara nueva del conjunto franjiverde y en el tercer fichaje realizado en este último día del mercado. Lemar, de 30 años, llegó al Atlético en 2018 procedente del Mónaco en una operación por la que el club rojiblanco pagó 72 millones de euros. Durante su etapa en el Metropolitano ha disputado 186 partidos oficiales, con 10 goles y 19 asistencias, y ha conquistado LaLiga 2020/21 y la Supercopa de Europa. Internacional absoluto con Francia, formó parte de la selección que se proclamó campeona del mundo en 2018. Su calidad técnica, visión de juego y capacidad para encontrar el último pase son sus principales argumentos. Con su llegada, el Elche suma además al segundo futbolista procedente del Atlético este verano, después de Javi Morcillo. El francés aportará experiencia y talento a un centro del campo que gana así un nuevo recurso ofensivo para la temporada en LaLiga EA Sports.

articles.title: El delantero Petar Ratkov, undécimo fichaje del Levante
articles.standfirst: El serbio llega al cuadro granota en forma de cesión procedente de la Lazio con una opción de compra condicionada
articles.summary: El serbio llega al cuadro granota en forma de cesión procedente de la Lazio con una opción de compra condicionada
articles.body: El Levante ha anunciado la incorporación de Petar Ratkov para la temporada 2026-27. El delantero serbio llega cedido por la Lazio hasta final de curso, en una operación que incluye una opción de compra, sujeta al cumplimiento de ciertas condiciones deportivas, según indicaba el club romano en su comunicado oficial. Con esta incorporación, el club valenciano añade una nueva alternativa para el ataque de Luis Castro, que contará con más recursos para aumentar el potencial ofensivo de la plantilla. Ratkov se suma a jugadores como Etta Eyong, Musuayi e Iván Romero, ampliando la competencia en una de las líneas que el Levante pretendía reforzar de cara a su regreso a la élite. El atacante, nacido en Belgrado el 18 de agosto de 2003, destaca por su imponente físico. Con 1,93 metros de altura, se trata de un delantero con capacidad para fijar centrales, dominar el juego aéreo y ofrecer variantes en los últimos metros. Ratkov se formó en las categorías inferiores del FK DIF Beograd antes de incorporarse al FK TSC Backa Topola, club desde el que dio el salto al fútbol europeo. En la temporada 2023-24 fichó por el Red Bull Salzburgo, donde comenzó a adquirir protagonismo internacional y debutó en competiciones como la Liga de Campeones y la Liga Europa. Durante su etapa en Austria protagonizó además uno de los episodios más destacados de su carrera. El 17 de febrero de 2024 marcó el gol más rápido de la historia de la Bundesliga austriaca al adelantar a su equipo frente al FC Blau-Weiß Linz apenas seis segundos después del saque inicial. Antes de llegar a Italia, Ratkov disputó 99 encuentros oficiales y anotó 22 goles con la camiseta del Red Bull Salzburgo. Su progresión llevó a la Lazio a incorporarlo en enero de este año, aunque su protagonismo en el conjunto romano fue limitado. De hecho, durante la campaña 2025-26 participó en nueve partidos oficiales, ocho de ellos en la competición liguera y uno en la copa nacional. A pesar de actuar como referencia ofensiva, no logró marcar ningún gol, una circunstancia que ha favorecido su salida en busca de más minutos y continuidad. El nuevo futbolista levantinista también cuenta con experiencia internacional. Ratkov ha sido habitual en las categorías inferiores de Serbia, defendiendo los colores de las selecciones Sub-19 y Sub-21, y debutó con la selección absoluta el 14 de octubre de 2023. Con su llegada, el Levante incorpora un delantero joven, con experiencia en competiciones europeas y margen de crecimiento, llamado a convertirse en una de las referencias ofensivas del equipo durante la presente temporada. El club confía en que su perfil físico y su capacidad para generar presencia en el área contribuyan a reforzar el potencial atacante de una plantilla que sigue tomando forma bajo la dirección de Luis Castro.

articles.title: Lincoln 0-0 Blackburn: Tom Atcheson sent off but 10-man Rovers earn point
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Lincoln City and Blackburn Rovers at the ProAmpac Stadium on Tuesday night; Tom Atcheson sent off but Tony Mowbray's away side earn a valuable point.
articles.body:
It was the first competitive fixture between the clubs at Sincil Bank since 1973.

But the Imps saw their chances of making it an impressive hat-trick of successive Championship wins go begging.

Both sides had chances, but it was ultimately a game lacking real quality in front of goal.

Tom Atcheson was sent off for a second bookable offence in the second half, a decision which left the Rovers bench incensed with the officials.

Lincoln are still waiting for their first home win since gaining promotion to the second tier, while Blackburn are yet to secure a victory on the road.

The Imps made two changes from the side which beat Bolton at the weekend as they went searching for their first home win in the Championship.

The returning Rob Street nodded an inviting Reeco Hackett free-kick over the bar on the 25-minute mark.

Rovers defender Ryan Alebiosu fired a strike over the bar after Sam Morsy's blocked volley fell into his path.

Freddie Draper could not quite turn Adam Reach's intelligent ball into the net as he poked wide on the stretch.

Blackburn playmaker Todd Cantwell saw his free-kick denied by a good George Wickens save from the best chance of the first half.

Rovers came firing out of the blocks after the break.

The visitors had the ball in the net early in the second half as Icelandic forward Andri Gudjohnsen saw his rebound chalked off with Cantwell, whose effort was blocked on the line, adjudged to have been offside earlier in the play.

Alebiosu had a shot deflected wide as Rovers continued to go close to breaking the deadlock.

A scramble from a corner inside the Rovers box saw Aynsley Pears produce a brilliant stop to keep out Dom Jefferies' effort.

Striker Gudjohnsen proved his worth inside his own box as he forced Draper's strike wide of the mark just before the hour.

Atcheson, booked early in the first half for a foul on Hackett, saw red when he chopped down Street with 21 minutes to go.

Deji Elerewe nodded wide from Hackett's cross before Ryoya Morishita was denied by Wickens down the other end heading into the final quarter of an hour.

Both sides had late chances as Isaac Olaofe pulled his shot wide for the hosts before Gudjohnsen headed off target from Jayden Fevrier's dinked ball in.

Conor McGrandles almost stole the spoils when he blasted over the bar for the hosts.

"We were as frustrated in the first 60-65 minutes than we were after the sending off where it becomes difficult to break them down.

"They were really resilient and they've had a couple of players really step up for them at the end there.

"We didn't have many glaring chances, but if we play that game 10 times I think we win it a lot of them. You can't be too disappointed with a point in the Championship.

"It became a bit snatchy, especially at the end. They're down to 10 men and we're trying to win the game. It's [not scoring] never through a lack of effort, if someone takes one it could possibly be a much easier evening.

"As I've said, you can't be too frustrated with a draw in the Championship. It's an ex-Premier League team coming to Sincil Bank and I thought we were the most threatening team throughout.

"We were incredibly solid in defence. It was a cat and mouse game. I think most fans will go home from that frustrated, you felt we'd score in those last 20 minutes, but the efforts and application can't be faulted."

"I'm frustrated, but also relieved with how we've come through that 20 minutes at the end.

"I'm a bit frustrated because at the start of the second half we started to open them up a little bit.

"We got behind them a few times, but didn't quite finish it. My hope was the longer the game went on the more openings there might have been for us.

"We'll take a point, it's a tough place to come. I think a lot of teams will find it tough here unless they can score first."

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Portsmouth 0-2 Derby: Sam Szmodics and Lars Jorgen Salvesen net in Rams win
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Portsmouth and Derby County at Fratton Park on Tuesday night; Sam Szmodics and Lars Jorgen Salvesen score as Rams claim their first win of the season.
articles.body:
Pompey dominated possession and had 19 shots to the Rams seven, but Josh Eustace's side were ruthless when it counted and deservedly left the south coast with three points.

Derby took the lead with their first meaningful attack in the 16th minute after an excellent run down the right from Bobby Clark saw him pull the ball back to Szmodics, who cleverly spun his defender and fired low into the near post.

Portsmouth were bossing possession and territory and Abu Kamara was screaming for a penalty when he tumbled under the challenge of Charlie Taylor, but referee Sam Allison ruled the Rams defender had played the ball.

John Mousinho handed a first start to Serbian striker Marko Milovanovic after the former Almeria player scored a late consolation penalty in Saturday's 2-1 defeat at Bristol City.

The six-foot five-inch forward was lively in the early stages and saw a low shot from the edge of the area comfortably saved by Jacob Widell Zetterstrom in the Derby goal.

But though they had 64 per cent of possession and 10 shots in the first half, that was Pompey's only effort on target.

Derby enjoyed a good spell of pressure at the start of the second half and the ebullient Clark put in a low cross which reached Sondre Langas on the edge of the six-yard box but the Norwegian was unable to get his shot away.

Pompey then came close to a fortuitous equaliser when Zak Swanson swung in a cross which almost caught out Zetterstrom at the far post before he clawed it behind.

From the resulting corner, Kamara saw his effort deflected narrowly wide of the Derby post.

But as Mousinho's men continued to push forward, gaps were appearing for Derby at the other end.

Derby boss Eustace had just brought on Salvesen for Rhian Brewster and with almost his first touch, the Norwegian scored his first goal since January as he received the ball from Oscar Fraulo and smashed it into the top corner from the edge of the area with his left foot.

The excellent Clark was continuing to cause problems and almost added a third as his teasing run from the left ended with a low shot that flashed just past the post.

Pompey have now lost both of their home games and, for all their pressure, Mousinho will be concerned that his side look so toothless in attack.

"We were really sloppy with some of the things that we did. We gave the ball away too easily and it ended in us conceding the second goal on a counter-attack again and not being able to get back in the game.

"We created a couple of half chances. We had some set pieces and I think the first attack Derby had and the only shot in the first half ends up in the back of the net. We have to be a lot better at coping with those specific moments and also coping with disappointment.

"I thought we reacted okay in the first half, but the second half, I didn't think we came out with any energy and any lively parts of our play."

"It's just about keeping your head, keeping your nerve, not getting carried away with all the noise and the distractions which come with it when you don't win games and you don't perform very well.

"We haven't been able to play a starting XI on any of our pre-season games or in any of our first three games.

"So, it's just about doing the right things, believing in what you do and believing in the process. And that's something I've always done over the course of my managing career and something I believe works.

"We're delighted to get our first three points of the season, but nothing's ever decided in the first month or two months. Last year we won one of our first 10 games and then we were 45 minutes away from finishing the play-offs. So, let's just keep believing in what we're doing."

articles.title: Birmingham 1-1 Southampton: August Priske heads in to earn a point for the Blues
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Birmingham City and Southampton at St Andrew's on Tuesday night; August Priske scores to peg back Saints and earn Chris Davies' Blues a point.
articles.body:
The Danish striker's neat header in the 55th minute cancelled out new signing Keven Schlotterbeck's towering aerial effort in the third minute of time added on at the end of the first half.

Birmingham should have had more for their efforts having had the lion's share of a glut of chances, with Jay Stansfield missing two sitters, including hitting the post.

In an end-to-end start, there were openings for both teams.

Saints striker Cyle Larin was put through by Finn Azaz only to finish poorly with a low drive straight at James Beadle.

Blues, who signed Hull winger Liam Millar on a season-long loan on deadline day, forced Daniel Peretz into a falling save from Priske's low drive.

Beadle's clearance was charged down by Azaz only for the ball to trickle wide as the visitors threatened.

Stansfield rattled the inside of the post after racing 40 yards following Schlotterbeck's mis-hit backpass.

Then, unmarked, the £10m striker headed inches wide from Alex Cochrane's cross.

Blues threatened again when Jhon Solis advanced only to fire just wide from 20 yards.

Larin lashed over the bar after Azaz's pass split the defence as the chances kept coming.

Cochrane's deep free kick gave Tomoki Iwata a sniff of goal at the far post but he sliced wide unmarked.

Priske's twisting header dropped just wide from Patrick Roberts' cross in another Blues raid.

But centre back Schlotterbeck made Blues pay for those missed opportunities by heading powerfully home from Leo Scienza's corner for his first goal since January 2025.

Roberts wriggled his way through for what home fans thought was the equaliser on 49 minutes only for Peretz to smother his shot.

But they did not have to wait much longer as Roberts crossed for Priske to guide home a header. It was the Danish striker's first league goal of the season.

Saints missed a double chance to regain the lead when substitute James Ward-Prowse's deflected shot was palmed upwards by Beadle and Larin looped the rebound wide.

Blues breathed a sigh of relief as Kuryu Matsuki's volley was ruled offside before Priske's rising shot flew just over.

Beadle palmed away Ward-Prowse's 25-yard free kick, James Bree firing the rebound into the sidenetting.

Phil Neumann headed straight at Peretz from Demarai Gray's free kick as Blues pressed for the winner.

"It was a very good game. We had an electric start - I was really pleased with how we got after them.

"Our tails were really up which is exactly what we want to be here, St. Andrew's was rocking.

"So to go in at half-time a goal down was a real sucker punch as they had had little periods of control with the ball without hurting us too much.

"We deserved to get the goal and could have won the match. August worked his socks off and was a real handful so it was great for him to score."

"It was a good advertisement for the Championship - a good game of football.

"There were a couple of moments that went in our direction to win it, but overall a very good quality Championship game.

"It was quite an even game - there were a couple of chances for us and the same for Birmingham.

"Fair play to Keven - it was a great header and a great delivery from Leo Scienza.

"It was a proper header, there is so much conviction in everything he does.

"I take that (error) on me because we try to play football and sometimes that can happen if the ball goes back and you try to find a solution.

"That one slipped through but I will take the blame for that.

"It was an excellent decision from Daniel Peretz not to come rushing out - it allowed the striker more time to think and delay the shot.

"It shows the courage and bravery in which he (Schlotterbeck) continued to play the game, especially in an atmosphere like this, so all credit to him."

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Stoke 1-0 Norwich: Ethan Galbraith earns vital win for Potters
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Stoke City and Norwich City at the bet365 Stadium on Tuesday night; Ethan Galbraith scores the only goal to earn a vital win for the Potters.
articles.body:
The Potters had lost all three of their opening league games, including Saturday's 4-1 loss at Wolves, conceding nine goals in the process.

Stoke had only won three times in the league since Norwich's 1-0 victory at the bet365 on January 4, a run of 23 games.

After picking up their first win of the season with an impressive 4-1 victory over Burnley on Saturday, Norwich were condemned to their third defeat in four matches, leaving them also with just three points.

The hosts were without talismanic winger Sorba Thomas as he closed in on a move to newly promoted Hull, as the Potters switched to a three-at-the-back system that saw Luke Graham and Million Manhoef included in the starting line-up.

Despite their dismal start to the season, Stoke had found themselves ahead in four of their five games in all competitions and did so again after 13 minutes through Galbraith.

Eric Bocat's low cross was deflected into the path of the ex-Manchester United midfielder, who unleashed a sweet strike from outside the box which cannoned off Jack Stacey and into the bottom corner.

It had been a slow start from the Canaries, but Philippe Clement's side sprung into life with 10 minutes remaining of the first half when Darlin Yongwa, starting a Championship game for the first time, stung the palms of Viktor Johansson.

Mohamed Toure and Andre Brooks had scored a brace each in Norwich's 4-1 rout against Burnley at the weekend and when they combined to set Brooks free one-on-one with Johansson, it looked destined to be 1-1.

The Swede stood firm and his outstretched right leg denied Brooks from seven yards out.

Canaries captain Kenny McLean then bent his effort inches wide of the post as Stoke were forced to endure a Norwich onslaught.

At the other end, it was Vladan Kovacevic's turn to pull off an impressive save as he stood tall to keep Manhoef out.

Brooks was then denied again by Johansson as an end-to-end first half was brought to a close.

Norwich had enjoyed over 70 per cent possession but had only mustered two second-half shots when Stoke almost caught them on the counter.

Substitutes Robert Bozenik and Sam Gallagher combined to play in deadline-day signing Luca Bombino, who cut inside and forced Kovacevic to tip his effort over the crossbar.

Norwich began to knock on the door when Oscar Schwartau blazed wide before McLean's deflected effort was pushed wide by Johansson, while the Sweden international also gathered Anthony Musaba's tame header.

The visitors had Ruairi McConville to thank as he slid in to prevent a certain Stoke second in the closing moments, but the Potters held on to claim a vital first victory of the season.

"I think you've seen the team galvanised, and they deserve an enormous amount of credit because we've not had the chance to work on a great deal.

"We've worked it, we've looked at things, not had too much chance to practise it, but I thought they stuck to the task pretty well.

"Let's face it, they had miles more of the ball but we know in this division it doesn't make any difference how much of the ball you have, so if you can't use the ball well enough then so what?

"But we are better than we have shown, and we tried to be better in the games that we've lost. This season we've started with three really difficult games.

"They deserve an enormous amount of credit because of the pressure around. Nobody's getting carried away, it's three points, but the manner of the performance and the way the supporters got behind the players was brilliant, and they really deserved that."

"I think all game we were the dominant team, the best team on the ball, the team getting the best chances.

"But you lose a game on a transition moment, and there were a few other transition moments that we defended really well.

"You need to win these games, and you need a little bit of luck in football, that's the case. For us, it's the job to prepare the team well so that we can be dominant, that we can create the most chances, that we can have most of the ball, but that's less important in general.

"In football you can also win games by having the best chances (while) having less possession.

"The possession difference was really big today, the creation of chances with Stoke was really big today, but they get the three points in the end and they are the cruel things that happen in football.

"One of those days, and frustrating, but you need to make a good analysis. I was very disappointed, close to angry, after our Millwall game because we didn't show our identity, we didn't play a good game or deserve the points, that was clear.

"Every neutral supporter will say that Norwich had to win this game, that's clear.

"You need to praise their goalkeeper also. He played a really good game with several good saves, so he played a really strong game and that stopped us also."

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Irish Premiership: 'I've got that spark back'- Conor McMenamin after Glentoran return
articles.summary: Conor McMenamin says his short-lived move to Coleraine "was not meant to be" after his shock deadline day return to Glentoran.
articles.body:
Conor McMenamin says his short-lived move to Coleraine "was not meant to be" after his shock deadline day return to Glentoran.

The 31-year-old joined the Bannsiders in June on a long-term deal from St Mirren but has now made an unexpected return to the Glens for his second spell at the club.

McMenamin scored 39 goals in 80 appearances for the east Belfast side before he moved to the Buddies in 2023.

"Before I went to Coleraine, Glentoran wasn't an option and, as soon as I found out that they were this time around, I said to my agent to get it done quick," McMenamin told BBC Sport NI's Stephen Watson.

"I'm delighted and I want to play with that smile and that freedom that I did before I came here.

"It's been pretty challenging the last two months for me, and I probably didn't really enjoy any of the last two months. Now I've got that spark back, I'm happy to be here, and I can't wait to get going."

McMenamin joins Glens two months after Coleraine move

McMenamin did not start a game for Coleraine during his short spell at the club and made three substitute appearances for the side in the Irish Premiership.

Despite the move failing to live up to the hopes that surrounded it, McMenamin added that it was "nobody's fault".

"It didn't work out at Coleraine and that is nobody's fault and I have no bad things to say about Coleraine," he continued.

"From a family and personal perspective, it was not meant to be. I am glad to be back here and playing football.

"I couldn't commit to living up there. It was too far to travel, and I have family in Downpatrick, and it just wasn't working out, and my partner is from Scotland. These things happen in football."

The Northern Ireland international made the move from the Glens to St Mirren in 2023 and made 64 appearances during his time at the Buddies.

He was also part of the St Mirren side that beat Celtic in the 2025-26 League Cup final.

Now, that experience of winning silverware is something that McMenamin hopes to bring back with him to the Glens.

"When I was in Scotland, I got a taste for winning trophies, and it was an unbelievable experience as a player, and this club deserves to win trophies," he continued.

"We have to be able to try and bring the league back here. That's what a big club should do and a big club should be ambitious to win trophies and I hope I can help fulfil that ambition.

"I'm here for a long time and, you know, I'm here to play well and I'm here to win games for Glentoran and I am excited for that."

McMenamin is also hopeful that the return to familiar surrounding may revive his international ambitions.

He has won 14 Northern Ireland caps but has not featured in a green and white shirt since June 2024.

The winger added that he has already spoken to Northern Ireland manager Michael O'Neill about his return to his former club and has no intention of closing the door on his international career.

"I actually spoke to Michael [O'Neill] about the move.

"That is something as a player that I'll never close the door on. It's the best memories of my career.

"I now need to do well for Glentoran before any of that happens. So, I'll just look forward and do well for Glentoran and hopefully Michael will ring my phone again."

articles.title: Carlos Álvarez se marcha al América de México
articles.standfirst: El jugador andaluz se va traspasado por 6+1 millones de los que el 30% se irá para el Sevilla
articles.summary: El jugador andaluz se va traspasado por 6+1 millones de los que el 30% se irá para el Sevilla
articles.body: Carlos Álvarez ya forma parte del pasado reciente del Levante. El futbolista andaluz ha sido traspasado al Club América de México por 6 millones fijos, más uno variable y el porcentaje de una futura venta. La salida del atacante se convierte en uno de los movimientos más importantes del verano para la entidad granota, que necesitaba generar ingresos en un mercado marcado por las exigencias económicas derivadas de su situación financiera. La operación ha sido fruto de una negociación en la que todas las partes han encontrado un punto de encuentro. Por un lado, el Levante obtiene una importante inyección económica que le permitirá ganar margen de maniobra a nivel presupuestario. Por otro, el futbolista da el salto a uno de los clubes más potentes y mediáticos del continente americano después de varias ventanas de mercado en las que despertó el interés de distintos equipos tanto nacionales como extranjeros. Además, el traspaso tendrá repercusiones positivas para el Sevilla, club en el que se formó Carlos Álvarez. La entidad hispalense conservaba un 30% de una futura venta, por lo que percibirá una parte significativa de la cantidad desembolsada por el conjunto mexicano. La marcha del atacante se suma a las recientes ventas de Carlos Espí, Kervin Arriaga y Kareem Tunde, confirmando una profunda reestructuración de la plantilla levantinista durante el presente mercado estival. En las últimas semanas, el nombre de Carlos Álvarez había estado en el centro de numerosos rumores debido a su valor de mercado y al interés que había despertado tras sus buenas actuaciones con la camiseta azulgrana. Natural de Sanlúcar la Mayor (Sevilla), el jugador llegó al Levante en agosto de 2023 procedente del Sevilla Atlético. Aunque inicialmente aterrizó en Orriols en unas condiciones económicas favorables para el club valenciano, el ascenso a Primera División activó una cláusula que obligó al Levante a abonar alrededor de 500.000 euros por sus derechos. Durante sus tres temporadas como granota, Carlos Álvarez se convirtió en una de las referencias ofensivas del equipo gracias a su creatividad, capacidad para jugar entre líneas y visión de juego. En total, ha disputado 105 partidos oficiales entre Liga y Copa, en los que ha firmado 14 goles, además de un número destacado de asistencias y acciones decisivas que contribuyeron al regreso del club a la máxima categoría. Su rendimiento y progresión le convirtieron en uno de los activos más valiosos del Levante. Ahora, con su traspaso al Club América, el futbolista inicia una nueva etapa en su carrera mientras el conjunto de Orriols obtiene una de las mayores ventas de los últimos años y un importante respaldo económico para afrontar los retos de la temporada en Primera División.

WWE superstar and Alabama graduate Oba Femi paid a visit to his alma mater's football team on Tuesday and spoke to the Crimson Tide as the squad gets ready for its 2026 season opener against East Carolina.

Femi was on Alabama's track-and-field team from 2019-2022 after transferring from Middle Tennessee State. He won the shotput title at both the SEC Indoor and Outdoor Track and Field Championships in 2021 and took home the indoor shotput title again in 2022 before graduating with a visual arts degree.

Femi has loudly announced his presence in the WWE after making his main roster debut last December. Since then, he posted the most eliminations at Royal Rumble (five, tied with eventual winner Roman Reigns) and beaten Brock Lesnar twice (at WrestleMania and SummerSlam).

He's only been on the losing end of a singles or tag team match once since arriving (to Lesnar at Clash in Italy back in May).

It's clear WWE has big plans for Oba Femi, who is now in a feud with another rising star in Bron Breakker. The two will clash at Sunday Night's Main Event in Atlanta on Sunday, Sept. 6.

One day earlier, Alabama will open its season at home vs. the ECU Pirates. Kickoff for head coach Kalen DeBoer's squad is set for noon ET.

articles.body: Unai Vencedor (25 años) ya es historia en el Athletic, club con el que tenía todavía un año más de contrato. El internacional sub21 se ha desvinculado de la entidad después de un verano controvertido: entrenó durante varios días al margen de sus compañeros fuera de Lezama por decisión del club y en el momento que el Athletic anunció qué dorsales tendría cada futbolista en la plantilla a Vencedor no se le entregó ninguno. Una vez rescindido ha firmado contrato por una temporada con el Burgos, con opción a renovarse por una campaña más. El centrocampista debutó en Primera División a las órdenes de Gaizka Garitano para más tarde ser un futbolista muy utilizado por Marcelino hasta el punto de ser habitual en las concentraciones de la selección española sub21. En este tiempo renovó su contrato hasta junio de 2027. El mismo contrato al que él y la entidad han decidido poner fin este 1 de septiembre. La carrera de Vencedor en el Athletic ha estado marcada por las cesiones. Ha disputado 82 partidos como león, pero ha jugado a préstamo en Eibar, Racing y Levante, que ha sido su último destino. Que el Athletic le tuviera entrenando este verano fuera de las instalaciones de Lezama fue motivo de enfado entre sus compañeros de la plantilla.

articles.title: Zian Flemming transfer: Ipswich sign Burnley forward on four-year deal
articles.summary: Ipswich sign Burnley forward Zian Flemming on a four-year deal for a reported £20m.
articles.body:
Ipswich have signed Dutch forward Zian Flemming from Burnley for £20m.

Flemming, 28, has penned a four-year deal with Ipswich.

The striker scored 11 times in the league for Burnley last season, who were relegated. He has netted three in the first four games of this campaign.

Ipswich boss Gary O'Neil said he had an "impressive" first season and he was "very pleased" to have brought him to Ipswich.

O'Neil said: "He has good quality and experience and has started the new season well, so is a great addition to the group as we strengthen the squad further."

After beating West Ham in August, Burnley boss Nicky Yayen urged Flemming, who joined them from Millwall for £7m in 2025, to stay .

Flemming said he was "proud" to sign for Ipswich, who beat Sunderland 2-1 in their first game after returning to the top flight before being thrashed 5-2 by Manchester United at the weekend.

He said: "I played in the Premier League last season and really enjoyed my first season at the top level, competing against the best players and teams in the world, so I am delighted to now be back in there with a great club like Ipswich."

Flemming becomes Ipswich's 12th signing of the summer.

articles.title: Brooke Norton-Cuffy to Hull from Genoa: How loans at Lincoln, Rotherham, Coventry and Millwall got him to the top
articles.summary: With Brooke Norton-Cuffy making a Transfer Deadline Day move to Hull from Genoa, Adam Bate speaks to the England Under-21 international's former coaches at Lincoln and Rotherham to find out why playing early was so important for his development...
articles.body:
It involved John Marquis, a big, strong centre-forward with vast experience in English football's lower leagues and a dominant figure in any dressing room. Given that he was over a decade older than the young Norton-Cuffy, keeping quiet was the easy option.

"We had taken John on loan from Portsmouth to Lincoln from January until the end of the season. In an analysis meeting after a game, John, who is quite a big character, was vocal, discussing things that we have to defend better and how we should not concede.

"Brooke, as an 18-year-old lad, just said, 'I agree John and what you are saying is right. However, if you had scored the two opportunities you had, it would not matter about us defending.' It was non-confrontational, just a guy speaking about football and how it is."

Norton-Cuffy has taken an unusual route from Arsenal's academy. That spell at Lincoln was the first of four domestic loan moves that also took in time at Rotherham United, Coventry City and Millwall before making the big switch to Serie A side Genoa.

"He has done really well in Italy, loving it there and learning the language," says O'Donnell. But that dressing-room tale from Lincoln perhaps offers some insight into why Norton-Cuffy takes these things in his stride. "He is a really interesting character."

O'Donnell was impressed for other reasons too. "You had to drag him off the training ground. His work ethic was unbelievable. He was really good and he has just grown and developed. He went back to Arsenal and then got the opportunity to go to Rotherham."

The Championship was a level up for Norton-Cuffy - and an education. O'Donnell sees him as "a right full-back or wing-back" but he was thrust into the latter role with the Millers. "The team was pretty regimented as a back three," Matt Taylor tells Sky Sports .

Taylor was Rotherham's manager at the time. "He did fantastically well in that first half of the season." But it was a grind. "Rotherham in the Championship is difficult if you are an 18-year-old kid with no real experience." Unsurprisingly, there were tough times too.

"He still showed what a good player he was but, physically, it just started to take its toll in the winter months," Taylor explains. "He would cramp up quite early. Playing wing-back was just quite a load for a young lad playing for Rotherham in the Championship."

It is hard to imagine Norton-Cuffy struggling with that. "You look at him now and he is quite a specimen, to be fair. He had the frame, he had the pace and the power. He is so dynamic and explosive." As they say, you win or you learn. And Norton-Cuffy learned.

"I really admire what he has done, going out to play games at such a young age when so many players stay in that academy system for too long. Then they eventually go out on loan when they are 20 or 21 and they find out about real football. He was doing it at 17."

So, what did he find out at Rotherham? "How to defend the back post. Full-backs at top academies are more comfortable in attacking situations. He learned his defensive responsibilities, opening the shoulders, knowing the dangers around you."

Taylor points out that this "probably set him in good stead for the next stage of his career" which came with a mid-season move to Coventry. Norton-Cuffy swapped a relegation battle with Rotherham for a promotion push with Mark Robins' Sky Blues.

"We wanted to keep him but I think Arsenal felt that playing for a better team, he might get more rhythm, which was probably true," admits Taylor. "At Rotherham, we were so bitty as a team at that level, it was so difficult for him." At Coventry, it was different.

Norton-Cuffy played in a Championship play-off final in front of over 85,000 people at Wembley before having a full season at Millwall. It was only after this that he made the permanent move from Arsenal to Genoa, adding to his football education in Serie A.

Italy is an examination more demanding of mind than body, still the most tactical league in Europe. A new language and culture, a higher standard of football, and plenty of highlights. The pick might have been a late winner with his left foot against Udinese.

Seeing Norton-Cuffy in Slovakia last summer at the European Under-21 Championship was to see the versatile game-changer that he has become. He came on as a substitute in both the semi-final and the final with the scores level. England won both matches.

He is no longer the green individual who nevertheless had the courage to challenge an experienced colleague at Lincoln. He is now ideally suited to the rigours of the Premier League. "His physicality and his experience is fantastic for his age," concludes Taylor.

"There is no reason why he cannot keep progressing. He is a hungry lad, who wants to learn and has been nicely managed so he is easily coachable as well. There is no reason why he cannot do well in the Premier League and become a full-grown international."

articles.title: El Manchester City convierte a Enzo Fernández en el fichaje más caro en la historia de la Premier
articles.standfirst: Los 'sky blues' pagarán 145 millones de euros por el mediocampista argentino
articles.summary: Los 'sky blues' pagarán 145 millones de euros por el mediocampista argentino
articles.body: Enzo Fernández (San Martín, 2001) cambia de bando. El 'culebrón' que envolvía al centrocampista argentino, de 25 años, ha llegado a su fin... sobre la bocina. El ex de River Plate y Benfica, vinculado al Real Madrid, deja el Chelsea para fichar por el Manchester City. Lo hace, eso sí, convertido en el traspaso más caro en la historia de la Premier League. El City ha igualado los 145 millones de euros que el Liverpool pagó el pasado verano al Newcastle por Alexander Isak. Es curioso. No es la primera vez que lo rompe. Los 121 millones que el Chelsea pagó al Benfica por él en enero de 2023 ya le convirtieron en su día en el fichaje más caro en la historia de la Liga inglesa. "Nos estamos preparando para todos los escenarios", advirtió Xabi Alonso, que sólo había utilizado 25 minutos a Enzo en lo que va de curso. Fue en la victoria sobre el Fulham (2-3) en la primera jornada de Liga. Ahora será otro Enzo, Maresca, el que lo vuelva a disfrutar. El argentino ya jugó 79 partidos a las órdenes del ex de Sevilla y Málaga en el Chelsea. No sólo eso. Sus buenos guarismos -marcó 15 goles y repartió 19 asistencias- ayudaron a los 'blues' a ganar la Conference League 2024-25 y el Mundial de Clubes 2025. Con Enzo, el gasto del City en fichajes este verano se dispara hasta los 456 millones. Nadie ha gastado más. Los 'sky blues' han pagado, además, 135 kilos por Elliot Anderson (Nottingham Forest), 95 por Ayyoub Bouaddi (Lille), 37,5 por Allan (Palmeiras), 25 por Mathys Detourbet (cedido al Mónaco), 11,7 por Jeremy Monga (Leicester), 3,5 por Gerónimo Rulli (Olympique de Marsella) y 3,5 por Pierce Charles (cedido al QPR). Es cierto que también han registado unos ingresos cuantiosos por ventas: 337,2 millones. El Chelsea, por su parte, bate el récord histórico de recaudación en una ventana de fichajes: 436,15 millones. Al traspaso de Enzo (145) hay que sumar todo lo que han recaudado por Andrey Santos (Man. United/56,3), Nico Jackson (Aston Villa/55,5), Marc Cucurella (Real Madrid/55), Liam Delap (Nottingham Forest/52,5), Trevoh Chalobah (Como/30), Tyrique George (Everton/21), Marc Guiu (RB Leipzig/15). Ha recibido, además, un total de 5,85 kilos por las cesiones de Benoit Badiashile (Nápoles), David Datro Fofana (Servette) y Dastan Satpaev (Burnley).

articles.title: El plantón del Mónaco deja a Xabi Alonso compuesto... y sin sustituto de Enzo Fernández
articles.standfirst: Subieron el precio de Lamine Camara cuando ya habían alcanzado un acuerdo
articles.summary: Subieron el precio de Lamine Camara cuando ya habían alcanzado un acuerdo
articles.body: compuesto y sin novia. El popular dicho popular bien podría aplicarse al peculiar cierre de mercado que ha vivido el Chelsea de Xabi Alonso. Los 'blues' acordaron el traspaso de Enzo Fernández al Manchester City a cambio de 145 millones de euros, récord en la historia de la Premier. Un pacto que el Chelsea acordó sabiendo que tenía cerrado a su sustituto: Lamine Camara (Diouloulou, 2004). El equipo que dirige Xabi Alonso apalabró el traspaso del internacional senegalés a cambio de 54,9 millones de euros aprovechando la necesidad de vender del equipo de El Principado después de que se torciera el traspaso de Folarin Balogun, también del Mónaco, al Everton. De pronto, al ver cómo el Everton reactivava su interés por fichar a Balogun, los del Principado cambiaron las condiciones y subieron el precio de Lamine Camara. "El Chelsea está furioso por la situación", aseguraba la 'BBC'. No es para menos. Los 'blues' habían llegado, también, a un acuerdo con el jugador para las próximas seis temporadas. Es curioso porque, según Kieran Gill, del 'Daily Mail', el Chelsea tuvo la oportunidad de echarse atrás y paralizar el traspaso de Enzo Fernández al Manchester City. A diferencia del Mónaco, prefirieron mantener su palabra y traspasar al argentino a cambio de 145 millones de euros. Una decisión que deja a Xabi Alonso compuesto... y sin Enzo. El Chelsea tendrá que salir adelante en la 'sala de máquinas' con Romeo Lávia, Moisés Caicedo,Jordan Henderson y los 'reconvertidos' Valentín Barco, Reece James y Malo Gusto.

articles.title: Arsenal fail to sign Julian Alvarez and with no elite attacker in, are Mikel Arteta's team short in the forward options?
articles.summary: Arsenal failed to bring in an elite attacker in the transfer window after going for Julian Alvarez, Vinicius Junior and Morgan Rogers; after selling four first-team forwards, are Arsenal short in attack this season - and has it opened up the title race?
articles.body:
After a summer-long transfer saga, Alvarez will now stay at Atletico Madrid after he tried to force through a move to Spanish rivals Barcelona, with Arsenal unsuccessful in convincing him to move back to the Premier League while waiting in the wings.

Speaking after the Champions League final defeat to Paris Saint-Germain, Arteta demanded Arsenal be "ambitious" and "fast" in the transfer market. The jury is very much out about whether Arsenal delivered on those two ambitions.

Arsenal started the summer with Rogers as their No 1 forward target. He went to Chelsea in a £117m, which Arsenal thought was too steep. They moved to an ambitious Vinicius Junior approach - but he stayed at Real Madrid.

Then came the Alvarez saga which ran right on until Deadline Day - but the Argentine never showed the desire to move to Arsenal. Christos Tzolis ended up being the only front three arrival at Arsenal this summer.

And despite that largely unsuccessful window in terms of the forward line, Arsenal still allowed Gabriel Martinelli, Leandro Trossard and Gabriel Jesus to leave - then also let Ethan Nwaneri join Borussia Dortmund on loan.

Four attackers out, one in. Are Arsenal putting their season at risk by being short in attack, not just in quality but in numbers too?

Left wing is a delicate area of the pitch, with Tzolis the only recognised player in that position between now and January.

Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke can fill in that position, but they are also tasked with providing cover and rotation for Martin Odegaard and Bukayo Saka in other areas of the Arsenal attack.

Eze showed after coming off the bench against Aston Villa that he can play in that left wing role and do a good job. But neither he nor Tzolis are really the pacy, one-on-one explorers that Arteta likes. Neither player tends to go in behind defences in the same way Martinelli used to.

Can Tzolis hold the left wing burden by himself for most of the season? Speaking to those who know him , one of his traits is the ability to recover from matches and go again three days later.

And at Club Brugge last season, Tzolis played just short of 4,400 minutes for the Belgian club. That's around 900 minutes short of what Martinelli and Trossard managed combined for Arsenal last season. On that basis, Tzolis may need to play around 10 more games this season compared to last - is that too many?

Another tense area of the pitch is centre forward. With Kai Havertz and Viktor Gyokeres in that area of the field and Jesus now departing, Arsenal are one player short in this position compared to last season.

Earlier this summer, Arteta revealed he feared the Premier League title had got away from Arsenal in November when the Gunners had just one striker available in Mikel Merino - who can of course fill in that role as well.

So weakening the centre-forward position looks a slightly peculiar decision, even though Jesus has barely featured for Arsenal in 2026.

Are there reasons for Arsenal to be positive?

Arsenal can say they have strengthened it without having to buy another player in the front three. The £75m signing of Bruno Guimaraes will add another dimension to the Gunners' attack.

Last season, the Brazilian was one of the top players in the Premier League at breaking the opposition backline - and put in an impressive cameo on his Premier League debut against Villa.

There is also the case of 16-year-old Max Dowman , who is set for a bigger role in the first-team compared to his 'wildcard' status last term. He could fill in at the right wing and No 10 roles while the likes of Madueke and Eze are needed elsewhere.

Arsenal also have enough in their squad for two players in every position - with some positions having three. The Gunners revolutionised their medical department over the summer, so if that leads to a better availability record for key players such as Saka and Odegaard, then that can add a new level to the forward line.

Part of Arsenal's excellent squad depth was addressing a concerning area of the team created by William Saliba's long-term injury, which forced them into the market for a new defender in Ezri Konsa .

With Jurrien Timber and Ben White not holding the best injury records - the latter even struggling against Villa on Monday night - that additional cover at right-back is useful.

In White, Konsa, Cristhian Mosquera and Piero Hincapie , Arsenal also possess a formidable back-up defence behind their regular back four - one that many Premier League teams would have as their first-choice backline.

But Man City have made some statement signings in this transfer window - revolutionising their midfield with Elliot Anderson, Ayyoub Bouaddi and Enzo Fernandez.

Chelsea did not just pinch Rogers away from Arsenal, but they also addressed several weak areas of their team - namely the goalkeeper, defence and experience sides of the squad.

Both those teams can say they are equipped to take on Arsenal in a title fight, while the Gunners can feel slightly disappointed with how their transfer window has gone from an attacking point of view.

Has the gap between Arsenal and the rest slimmed down? That question will be put under the microscope straight away on Sunday.

articles.title: Summer transfer spending: Premier League, EFL, WSL, Scottish Premiership, LaLiga, Ligue 1, Serie A and Bundesliga breakdowns
articles.summary: From England's top four divisions to LaLiga, Serie A, Bundesliga, Ligue 1, Scottish Premiership and Women’s Super League - we break down how much clubs spent in the 2026 summer transfer market across the continent
articles.body:
Figures subject to change with deal sheets.

Premier League clubs have smashed the transfer spending record after splashing £3.48bn on new signings.

The previous record of £3.19bn, set last summer, was surpassed following another extraordinary window across the top flight.

Clubs also recouped £2.17bn from player sales, contributing to a combined net spend of £1.30bn.

Premier League spending has now exceeded £2bn in each of the last five summer windows, with expenditure accelerating dramatically since 2022/23.

This summer's record outlay is almost three times the amount clubs spent a decade ago, when the 2016/17 total stood at £1.19bn.

The record has been broken despite Premier League clubs also generating another huge sum through sales, underlining the remarkable volume of money moving through the division.

Manchester City spent a league-high £440.3m during the window, followed by Chelsea (£342.4m), Spurs (£334m) and Newcastle (£275.2m).

In terms of net spend, Liverpool topped the table with £219.4m, followed by Ipswich (£190.7m), Spurs (£176m) and Arsenal (£136.6m).

At the other end of the scale, Chelsea finished the window £67.3m in profit after generating £409.7m from player sales.

Manchester City signed Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea for a joint-Premier League record £125m, matching Alexander Isak's move from Newcastle to Liverpool last summer.

Bradley Barcola (£123m) and Morgan Rogers ( £117m) were also among the window's biggest moves, while Elliot Anderson joined Manchester City for £116m and Sandro Tonali joined Spurs for £100m.

The scale of the market was reflected at the very top end: 20 players moved to Premier League clubs for fees of £50m or more.

Premier League clubs were also active sellers, with several of the summer's biggest transfers involving players moving either between English clubs or overseas.

Hull were the busiest recruiters, completing 17 permanent signings, followed by Ipswich (16), Chelsea (13), Brighton (12) and Coventry (11).

Meanwhile, Brighton shipped a league-high 24 players out on permanent deals, ahead of Aston Villa and Crystal Palace (23) and Ipswich (21).

Championship clubs also set a new summer spending record, with expenditure reaching £289.3m.

That comfortably eclipsed the previous high of £204.2m, set last summer.

However, clubs recouped £461.4m from player sales, meaning the division collectively registered a transfer profit of £172.1m.

Stoke , Wrexham and Norwich recorded the highest net spends in the division, while West Ham , Burnley and Southampton generated the biggest transfer profits.

The promoted and relegated clubs helped drive some of the largest numbers.

But the division continues to be an important seller of talent: Championship clubs have collectively generated a transfer profit every summer since 2016/17.

You can use the interactive tables below to find every signing and outgoing involving League Two clubs this summer.

The Scottish Premiership transfer window remains open until September 3 at 5pm, so the figures below will continue to update.

The WSL transfer window remains open until September 3 at 11pm, so the figures below will continue to update.

Premier League clubs have again comfortably outspent their counterparts across Europe's other major domestic leagues.

Serie A clubs spent £843.6m, followed by LaLiga ( £603.1m), Bundesliga (£507.6m) and Ligue 1 (£490.6m).

But the picture changes significantly when sales are factored in.

Serie A recorded the highest net spend at £267.1m, while Ligue 1 clubs collectively generated a transfer profit of £467m after recouping £957.6m from player sales.

The contrast with the Premier League is considerable: English top-flight clubs have spent around four times as much as Serie A this summer.

However, Europe's major leagues remain a crucial source of Premier League recruitment, while substantial fees have also flowed in the opposite direction.

Real Madrid have the highest net spend outside the Premier League at £143.8m, followed by Juventus (£118.2m) and Fiorentina (£104.6m).

Yan Diomande is the most expensive signing across Europe's other leading leagues, completing a £107.1m move from RB Leipzig to Real Madrid ( Sky Sports fee: £120m ).

articles.summary: El central austríaco abandona el club tras dos temporadas
articles.body: El Elche ha hecho oficial la salida de David Affengruber, que se marcha al Fulham después de que ambos clubes hayan alcanzado un acuerdo para su traspaso. La operación se cierra por una cantidad cercana a los 12 millones de euros, convirtiéndose en una de las ventas más importantes de la historia reciente del conjunto franjiverde. El defensa austríaco pone fin a una etapa de dos temporadas en el Martínez Valero, en las que ha sido protagonista de uno de los capítulos más destacados del Elche en los últimos años. Affengruber llegó al club en Segunda División y rápidamente se convirtió en uno de los pilares de la defensa que terminó consiguiendo el ascenso a LaLiga EA Sports. Su importancia se mantuvo durante la temporada 2025/26, en la que volvió a ser una pieza fundamental para alcanzar el objetivo de la permanencia en Primera División. A sus 25 años, el central deja el Elche para afrontar una nueva aventura en la Premier League. Su rendimiento, carácter competitivo y regularidad han provocado que el Fulham apueste fuerte por su incorporación. El Elche pierde así a uno de los hombres importantes de su defensa, pero obtiene a cambio una importante inyección económica. Affengruber se marcha dejando un buen recuerdo entre la afición franjiverde después de contribuir directamente a dos objetivos históricos: el regreso a Primera y la permanencia.

articles.title: Lamine Camara: Monaco pull out of selling midfielder to Chelsea in £47m deal after Blues agreed deal for Enzo Fernandez replacement
articles.summary: Chelsea were looking for a midfield addition after letting Enzo Fernandez join Man City in a £125m deal, which is a joint-record for a British club; Monaco pulled out because they successfully renegotiated a deal to sell Folarin Balogun to Everton only for the deal to fall through
articles.body:
Camara was set to join Chelsea for £47m and was to sign a six-year deal pending a medical.

Just after the 11pm transfer deadline passed, news emerged that Monaco reneged on the agreement they had with Chelsea, and they had informed the Blues of their decision in writing.

The reason for Monaco pulling out was that they had successfully renegotiated the deal to sell Folarin Balogun to Everton, but the striker sensationally backed out of the move at the very last minute.

Monaco only wanted to sell one player, and once they thought they had a deal agreed to sell Balogun to Everton, they pulled out of the Camara-to-Chelsea deal despite a full written club-to-club agreement with the Blues.

Monaco refused to sign a Camara deal sheet before the 11pm deadline, and there is no chance of Chelsea resurrecting a deal for the Senegal international.

The feeling at Chelsea towards Monaco now is likely to be "what goes around comes around".

Chelsea had been looking for a new midfielder with Enzo Fernandez joining Manchester City in a joint-British-record £125m deal.

Chelsea had the option of pulling the plug on Fernandez's move to Man City after the Camara deal had collapsed, but they stuck to their word and honoured their commitment to complete the deal.

Roma's Manu Kone was also shortlisted as a potential option, while Chelsea were also looking at midfield options in the Premier League.

"Enzo Fernandez is going to be a Manchester City player. Lamine Camara to Chelsea collapsing is totally separate.

"Chelsea have not been able to sign a replacement. Chelsea are really unhappy with the way Monaco behaved.

"My information is everything was done - written, agreed, signed. He was flying into London [on Wednesday].

"At the same time, Monaco have been negotiating with Everton to sell Folarin Balogun. Once they have agreed a deal with Everton, they have come back to Chelsea and gone back on their agreement.

"Chelsea don't believe this is the way clubs should conduct business. I suppose this is one of the risks you take when you leave things so late."

Chelsea goalkeeper Robert Sanchez has completed a season-long loan move to Serie A side Como .

The goalkeeper had been bumped down to Stamford Bridge following the arrival of Emi Martinez from Aston Villa .

Elsewhere, midfielder Dario Essugo has completed a season-long loan move to sister club Strasbourg . Essugo was of interest to Hull in this window.

Striker Deivid Washington has completed a permanent transfer to Strasbourg. He signed from Santos for £17.1m three years ago but made only three appearances.

Forward Dujuan Richards has also joined Wimbledon on a season-long loan.

Meanwhile, Chelsea striker Shim Mheuka has arrived in Glasgow ahead of his loan move to Celtic, who are also working to finalise a deal for Chelsea left-back Landon Emenalo.

articles.title: Enzo Fernandez: How Man City completed £125m deal for Chelsea midfielder
articles.summary: The summer's longest-running transfer saga ends with Manchester City paying a joint-British record fee to bring in midfielder Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea.
articles.body:
Manchester City 's desperation to bring in midfielder Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea not only ends the summer's longest running transfer saga but highlights the club's determination to get the deal done for manager Enzo Maresca's top target.

City have paid a joint-British record £125m deal for the Argentina international to break their club record transfer fee for the second time this summer following the £116m arrival of Elliot Anderson.

City had to overcome numerous obstacles to finalise a difficult deal during the 79-day transfer window, from being set deadlines to complete the deal and the backdrop of former Chelsea boss Maresca's acrimonious appointment as their manager.

But shelling out a joint-British record fee showcased City's perseverance to acquire their man and those upstairs at Etihad Stadium have shown unequivocal faith to both player and manager.

City have started the season with back-to-back Premier League wins and Fernandez's arrival means he becomes the first player in football history to move for more than £100m twice after going to Chelsea from Benfica for £107m in 2023.

The 25-year-old also joins a unique trio of players that have broken the British transfer record twice in their careers during the Premier League era along with former England internationals Alan Shearer and Rio Ferdinand.

All that means City's acquisition of Fernandez matches the amount paid by Liverpool to Newcastle for striker Alexander Isak on the same day last summer.

How have City pulled off the biggest deal of the summer despite a seemingly bitter relationship with Chelsea following the appointment of Maresca as manager earlier this summer?

Man City agree £125m deal for Chelsea's Fernandez

When Maresca was appointed as Pep Guardiola's replacement in June, the Italian apologised to his former club Chelsea for the "disruption" caused by his mid-season departure.

Senior City sources had told BBC Sport at the time that they held no ill feeling towards Chelsea and that the now-resolved contractual dispute was between the Stamford Bridge club and Maresca.

And that has played out in this deal happening.

The manager was the key factor in this blockbuster deal with Maresca keen to reunite with his former Chelsea skipper.

It is understood Maresca wanted Fernandez as someone who he can fully trust and rely on, a player that is familiar with the manager's instructions, the patterns of play and does not need to be learn how to operate in the middle of the park in the system.

The 46-year-old had a similar approach when being appointed as Chelsea manager in 2023, signing Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall having worked with the player at Leicester during their Championship-winning campaign.

Looking back on Friday's pre-match news conference, Maresca had hinted at a late incoming by saying he was hoping to add "a captain" to his squad before the end of the transfer window.

City have lost the experience of Bernardo Silva, John Stones and Rodri this summer, with Ruben Dias taking the captain's armband and Erling Haaland being part of the leadership group.

Fernandez adds big-game know-how to City's midfield after winning the 2022 World Cup with Argentina, being named young player of the tournament, and helping his country to a second-straight final in July.

His antics during the summer may not make him a universally popular figure but Fernandez comes across as a player that team-mates love to have alongside them and one that gets under the skin of the opposition players and supporters.

City had been interested in signing Chelsea 's Pedro Neto and Malo Gusto earlier this summer but were seemingly put off by the respective asking prices and, at that stage, Fernandez was not a player that Maresca had necessarily asked the hierarchy to sign.

However, the departures of Rodri, Tijjani Reijnders and Nico Gonzalez meant there was a gaping hole left in the middle of the park that needed filling.

Eyebrows were raised when Maresca deployed centre-back Marc Guehi in a holding midfield role in the opening game against Bournemouth , with the player himself saying he was surprised by the change in position.

That alteration came about as the deal for Morocco international Ayyoub Bouaddi had not been completed, so Guehi played alongside fellow England international Anderson.

The ownership have now splashed out £125m on Fernandez and deemed it as being worth the hefty fee for their new manager - they can also point to delivering a player who could be the final tool needed for Maresca and his men to challenge on all four fronts this season.

Though City claimed a domestic cup double in Guardiola's final season in charge, they fell short in the Premier League and Champions League so Maresca will now be under pressure to fare better in both of those competitions.

Under Maresca at Chelsea , Fernandez helped the club win the 2025 Europa Conference League and the Club World Cup later that summer but noises emerged at the start of this year about him wanting to leave.

It began once Maresca left Stamford Bridge in January and two months later, following Chelsea 's Champions League exit, Fernandez said he did not know whether he would be at the club next season.

His first choice was to join Real Madrid but the La Liga giants never came in with an offer, feeling the Premier League midfielder was overpriced.

New Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso spoke to Fernandez this summer in an attempt to try and change his mind and for him to stay, but the player's heart was set on leaving.

Having been jeered by his own supporters during the home pre-season friendly against Real Sociedad, there was only one direction of travel thereafter and that exit was seemingly rubberstamped after being left out of the wins over Luton and Brighton .

A deal with City was finally struck with just hours remaining in the transfer window, but which club will feel they came out on top?

Chelsea had set an arbitrary deadline of 14 August for clubs to match their £120m valuation of the player - which passed without any offers coming in - and they were understood to be holding out for £135m on Monday.

City had indicated they would walk away from the deal at the price, instead offering £125m the following day, which was subsequently accepted.

City got their man, while Chelsea received £5m more than what they initially asked for.

Chelsea have now raised more than £425m through player sales, including add-ons this summer and fees from loan deals are expected to take that figure closer to £500m.

Club sources initially indicated they would bank the cash and not bring in a direct replacement but, with time running out on deadline day, they performed an extraordinary pivot by agreeing a £47m deal to sign Monaco's Lamine Camara.

But there was one final twist at 23:00 BST as the window closed, with the Ligue 1 side reneging on the written agreement after renegotiating a deal to sell USA striker Folarin Balogun to Everton .

It left Chelsea with the Fernandez cash in their pocket but without a replacement and, though they could have pulled the plug on the deal, the Blues decided to honour their word and allowed him to join City.

articles.title: USMNT star Folarin Balogun staying at Monaco after reportedly walking away from Everton deal
articles.summary: Folarin Balogun reportedly failed a physical after a deal with Everton was agreed to.
articles.body:
Folarin Balogun is remaining with Monaco after all.

After it looked like a massive deal was in place to send the United States men's national team forward to Everton, the deal fell apart on Tuesday ahead of the English transfer window closing.

Balogun reportedly failed the physical, according to Give Me Sport's Ben Jacobs . That led to Everton renegotiating the terms of the deal, and then Balogun apparently opted to walk away. So, he'll stay with the Ligue 1 side instead.

Multiple reports indicated Monday that Monaco and Everton had agreed to a deal around €45 million ($52.3 million USD), plus around €5 million ($5.8 million) in potential add-ons.

Balogun had reportedly agreed to a four-year deal with a one-year option.

The move came just before the Premier League's summer transfer window closed on Tuesday, with Everton hoping to start the season with an enhanced attack. In a seemingly related move, Everton also agreed to bring back Manchester City's Jack Grealish for another season on loan, per multiple reports .

Balogun was excellent for Monaco last year, scoring 19 goals and adding 5 assists across all competitions. The striker notched nine goals in Monaco's final 12 games of the regular season, though the French heavyweight finished the year in seventh. Balogun ended the year fourth in Ligue 1's individual scoring table.

Balogun's club showing was buoyed by a breakout showing in the USMNT's World Cup run this summer. Though marred by the red card controversy surrounding his foul during a win over Bosnia and Herzegovina , Balogun finished the tournament with three goals on the way to the USA's largest World Cup win and its first knockout stage win in more than two decades.

The move would have marked a return to England for Balogun, who was raised in London, grew up in Arsenal's academy and started his career with the Gunners before heading to France in 2023. The 25-year-old forward's U.S. eligibility stems from his birth in New York City after his mother was barred from returning to England due to being too far along in her pregnancy.

Balogun would have been the latest USMNT player to earn a splashy transfer after breaking out at the 2026 World Cup, too. Midfielder Sebastian Berhalter, who played in all five U.S. World Cup matches after becoming an unlikely mainstay of the USMNT, was transferred from the Vancouver Whitecaps to Championship League side Middlesbrough in July. Defender Max Arfsten joined him a week later .

Sunderland Director of Football Florent Ghisolfi says new signing Malick Fofana possesses "all the attributes to thrive in the Premier League".

The Black Cats have beaten Crystal Palace to the signing of Fofana - who had previously been linked with Arsenal - from Lyon in a deal worth £30m.

The forward becomes Sunderland's fifth signing of the summer and has agreed a long-term deal at the Stadium of Light.

"Malick has all the attributes to thrive in the Premier League," said Ghisolfi.

"He is a player with huge potential and Sunderland AFC will provide him with the right environment to continue to develop and prosper."

Fofana began his career at KAA Gent before joining Lyon in 2024. He scored 19 goals and provided eight assists in 84 appearances for the Ligue 1 side.

"He operates off the left and will complement the versatility of the other wide men we have at the club, who can play across both flanks," Ghisolfi added.

"We are delighted to welcome Malick to the club and look forward to supporting him as he takes the next steps in his career."

Crystal Palace have completed the signing of Quinten Timber from Marseille , with the midfielder joining the Premier League club ahead of the transfer deadline.

The 25-year-old has signed a contract until 2031 after leaving Marseille just months after arriving at the French club in January. Marseille's financial problems have forced them to part with several key players this summer.

Timber has long been linked with a move to England, particularly since his twin brother Jurrien joined Arsenal in 2023. He now follows his sibling to the Premier League after establishing himself as a major player in the Netherlands.

The midfielder enjoyed a successful spell with Feyenoord , winning the Eredivisie and Dutch Cup while also serving as club captain. He was part of the Netherlands squad at this summer's World Cup and has earned 13 international caps.

Timber becomes the latest addition to Pierre Sage 's Palace squad as the Eagles strengthen ahead of the new Premier League and Europa League campaigns.
