articles.title: Transfer Deadline Day brings record spending but will any money be enough for these Premier League clubs?
articles.summary: Premier League spending shows no signs of abating as Transfer Deadline Day delivers record-breaking numbers. Adam Bate looks at how it unfolded and where it leaves Premier League clubs and supporters with the window now shut - but everyone still wanting more...
articles.body:
Premier League clubs spent more on players than in any transfer window in the sport's history. City's spending reached £440m but they brought in £315m. Chelsea spent £342m and brought in even more. Money flowing in and out at unprecedented levels.

Fernandez embodies the escalation in microcosm. Three-and-a-half years ago, his signing for £106.8m was held up as an example of excess. Now, Chelsea have a profit. Ditto Liam Delap . Maybe the signings of this summer will be the bargains of tomorrow.

And it was not just one or two clubs. The scale and depth was staggering. Even beyond the record-breaking deals, Liverpool added goalkeeper-for-the-future Lucca Brughmans for a fee that could rise to £30m. This would match Borussia Dortmund's record signing.

Brentford made a £40m signing, Brighton went as high as £50m. Had Coventry City signed their players in a particular order this summer then they could have broken their transfer record on five separate occasions. Ipswich Town signed a World Cup winner.

Fulham paid £34m for a Real Madrid striker. Tottenham's spending topped £300m. Aston Villa hit similar numbers while completely rebuilding their squad. That mood of renewal most conspicuous at Villa Park was a theme of the Premier League summer.

So many teams are in flux, underlined by the fact that Roberto De Zerbi is one of only nine coaches who took charge of their current club in the Premier League last season - and he did not arrive at Spurs until the end of March. Squads are being reshaped.

It explains some of what we have seen. Oliver Glasner linking up with Daniel Munoz again at Nottingham Forest . Pierre Sage trying, but failing, to persuade former player Malick Fofana to ditch Sunderland for Crystal Palace in one of the more colourful tales.

Fernandez's own reunion with Enzo Maresca did come off, sparking a late flurry of excitement in the window as Chelsea sought to replace the midfielder. The number of moving parts throughout this transfer window was a feature of the drama in the final days.

Wingers were a focus. Bradley Barcola was the biggest signing of the summer - for a day. Spurs were linked with Iliman Ndiaye but Man City swooped. They pivoted to Mykhailo Mudryk . Leeds had to move on, opting for Jean-Matteo Bahoya instead.

Newcastle signed Matias Fernandez-Pardo from Lille in a move that was confirmed at the relatively civilised hour of 3pm in the afternoon. Routine by Transfer Deadline Day standards. The French club had already sold Ayyoub Bouaddi to Man City for £81.3m.

Those selling clubs can seem like unlikely kingmakers in key moments. Monaco could knock back Chelsea's bids for Lamine Camara in the belief that Folarin Balogun was being sold to Everton . When that move stalled, Chelsea's hopes were reignited.

Cue the unexpected twists, an essential element of any classic Transfer Deadline Day. Chelsea were left frustrated as Monaco pulled out of the Camara deal. Then Balogun fell through too. Why do these multi-million moves have to go down to the wire?

Dashed ambitions and deal sheets, options and obligations, the moves that came off and those that did not. Once the dust settles, one wonders whether some will be uncertain that they have done enough. Others might even have buyer's remorse.

Will any of it work? Manchester City have broken the British transfer record only twice, for Steve Daley in 1979 and Robinho in 2008. The two men mustered 18 league goals for the club between them. Spending guarantees an impact on the accounts not the pitch.

And while the buzz that buying brings is a proven psychological phenomenon, the striking thing about this summer's spree is that so many supporters emerge from it still underwhelmed. However much money is committed, for some, it never feels enough.

Liverpool are still without a fit specialist right-back and with doubts over their midfield balance. Manchester United were unable to acquire the left-back that many regarded as essential. Even Arsenal fans are mumbling about being short up front.

Any answers now must be found on the pitch not in the market. With apologies to Tottenham, the onus is back on winning football matches not transfer windows. But never fear because the countdown is on. We get to do it all over again in January…

articles.title: Bundesliga loan roundup | Union Berlin, Stuttgart, and Leverkusen youngsters secure moves
articles.summary: Three Bundesliga clubs have confirmed outgoing developmental loans at the conclusion of the summer transfer window, with Union Berlin’s Oluwaseun Ogbemudia r...
articles.body:
Three Bundesliga clubs have confirmed outgoing developmental loans at the conclusion of the summer transfer window, with Union Berlin's Oluwaseun Ogbemudia returning to Waldhof Mannheim, Stuttgart youngster Mirza Catović heading to Barcelona and Bayer Leverkusen defender Jeanuel Belocian moving to Racing Santander.

Union Berlin have sent highly-rated young centre-back Oluwaseun Ogbemudia back to 3. Liga side Waldhof Mannheim on loan for the 2026/27 campaign. The 20-year-old already spent the second half of last season in Mannheim and established himself as an important performer. Union and Waldhof have now agreed to extend that developmental arrangement for another full season.

The four-times-capped German youth international returns to familiar surroundings at a club where regular senior minutes should remain available.

As detailed in Get German Football News's 2026/27 Union Berlin tactical preview , first-team opportunities in Köpenick remained difficult to forecast amid Union's established defensive options. Another season of consistent 3. Liga football therefore offers Ogbemudia a clearer route to continued development.

Stuttgart extend Catović before Barcelona loan

VfB Stuttgart have taken a different approach with 19-year-old Mirza Catović. The midfielder has extended his existing Stuttgart contract by one year through June 2029 before joining FC Barcelona's second team on a season-long loan. Stuttgart thus retain long-term control over the youngster while allowing him to continue his development in one of European football's most prominent academy environments.

VfB Board Member for Sport Fabian Wohlgemuth said the objective is for Catović to "gain further experience" during his year in Catalonia.

The move also makes sense within the context of Stuttgart's exceptionally deep senior squad.

Get German Football News's 2026/27 Stuttgart tactical preview highlighted the abundance of options available to Sebastian Hoeneß throughout the centre of the pitch. With Stuttgart competing at the upper end of the Bundesliga and returning to Champions League football, Catović's immediate route to regular first-team minutes remained narrow.

The Barcelona loan now supplies him with a significantly different developmental challenge without weakening Stuttgart's contractual position.

Leverkusen send Belocian to Racing Santander

Bayer Leverkusen have meanwhile confirmed that Jeanuel Belocian will spend the season on loan with Spanish top-flight side Racing Santander. The 21-year-old defender, recently returned from a Wolfsburg loan, moves without a reported purchase option and remains firmly part of Leverkusen's longer-term plans.

Competition for defensive minutes had become particularly fierce following another summer of heavy personnel turnover at the BayArena.

Belocian nevertheless featured regularly during preseason. As noted in Get German Football News's 2026/27 Bayer Leverkusen tactical preview , the Frenchman scored in the 4-0 friendly victory over Genk and received opportunities under new head coach Carles Martínez as Leverkusen experimented with several defensive combinations.

The increasingly crowded squad nevertheless made consistent competitive minutes difficult to guarantee.

Leverkusen sporting managing director Simon Rolfes made clear that the loan should not be interpreted as the club moving on from Belocian.

"Upon his return next year, he will be a promising candidate for our Werkself," Rolfes said.

articles.title: Everton sell Scotland's Nathan Patterson to Torino
articles.summary: Everton sell Scotland right-back Nathan Patterson to Torino for an undisclosed fee.
articles.body:
Everton have sold Scotland right-back Nathan Patterson to Torino for an undisclosed fee.

The 24-year-old joined the Premier League club from Rangers for a reported £12m on five-and-a-half-year contract in January 2022 but failed to become a regular starter.

Patterson did make 68 appearances during an injury-hit time with Everton, 29 of those as a substitute, eight of them last season.

He meantime appeared six times for Scotland and, having played in all three of their World Cup group games, returned to Everton hoping to finally establish himself as a first-team regular under fellow Scotsman David Moyes.

However, the defender made his first and only appearance this season as a second-half replacement in last week's 4-0 League Cup win away to Preston North End.

Patterson, who has 29 caps, joins international colleague Che Adams at Torino, the striker himself having been the subject of summer transfer speculation.
